key_insight: Fuse-PINN combines finite-element methods with physics-informed neural networks to enable scalable multi-GPU simulations of nonlinear PDEs.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a route to large-domain, fine-scale nonlinear physics simulation on GPU-based HPC systems, demonstrated for magnetic-confinement fusion rather than solid mechanics.
method: Formulates a finite-element method for neural networks (FEM-NN).
Implements FEM-NN in a modular framework for parallel GPU execution.
Uses Energy Natural Gradient Descent for high-precision convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-perfect scaling as problem size increases across multiple GPUs, with demonstrations including nonlinear convective models with fine-scale dynamics.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify GPU counts, accuracy, or speedups over conventional FEM solvers, leaving practical performance gains to be assessed.
paper_title: Fuse-PINN: Combining Finite Element Methods and Physics-Informed Neural Networks to enable massively parallel simulations of non-linear PDEs
